description: Lemon, lime, grapefruit, white peach and green apple with orange blossom and a saline, sea-spray finish. Light pithy bitterness.
notes: Usually no wood aging. Atlantic influence keeps acidity high.
confusion: Sauvignon Blanc shows pyrazine and green herbs; Chablis has more chalk and less floral fruit; Pinot Grigio is more neutral.

description: Green apple, pear and lemon with oyster shell, chalk and wet stone. Lean and taut with racy acidity.
notes: Kimmeridgian limestone. Most Petit Chablis and village wines see no new oak; some Premier and Grand Cru see a little.
confusion: Albariño is more floral and saline-citrus; Loire Sauvignon Blanc has pyrazine; dry Chenin Blanc shows wax and quince.

description: Ripe apple, pear and lemon with hazelnut, mushroom, wet stone and subtle toast and cream from oak and lees.
notes: Meursault is richer and nutty; Puligny is more mineral; Mâconnais is fruitier with less oak.
confusion: California Chardonnay is riper with more butter and oak; Chablis is leaner with no oak influence.

region: Napa Valley, Sonoma County & Central Coast, California
description: Baked apple, pineapple, mango and lemon curd with butter, vanilla, toast and baking spice. Full-bodied and creamy.
notes: Full malolactic fermentation and new oak are common, though cooler Sonoma Coast sites make leaner styles.
confusion: Viognier is more floral with lower acid; oaked Sauvignon Blanc keeps a herbal note and higher acid.

description: Quince, apple, pear and lemon with chamomile, lanolin and beeswax, honey and chalky minerality. Piercing acidity.
notes: Vouvray ranges from sec to demi-sec; Savennières is dry, fuller and more oxidative.
confusion: Chablis lacks the wax and honey; Alsace Riesling shows petrol and more citrus; Pinot Gris is lower in acid.

description: Lychee, rose petal, apricot, pink grapefruit and Turkish delight with ginger and sweet spice. Oily texture, low acid, phenolic finish.
notes: One of the most aromatic grapes; often finished with a little residual sugar.
confusion: Viognier is less rose-scented and more stone fruit; Torrontés is lighter with higher acid and a bitter edge.

description: Baked apple, ripe pear and peach with honey, ginger, smoke and wet stone. Rich, oily texture.
notes: Often a touch of residual sugar. Grand Cru sites add smoky minerality.
confusion: Chenin Blanc has higher acid and wax; Alsace Riesling is leaner with petrol; Pinot Grigio is much lighter.

description: Pear, green apple, lemon and white peach with almond skin and a light mineral, slightly bitter finish. Light-bodied and neutral.
notes: Friuli examples can be fuller with some skin contact; Alto Adige is crisp and alpine.
confusion: Albariño is more saline and floral; Chablis has more chalk and acid; Alsace Pinot Gris is much richer.

description: Lime, green apple, white peach and apricot with petrol, honey, blossom and slate. Feather-light alcohol and searing acidity balancing any sweetness.
notes: Trocken is dry; Kabinett and Spätlese usually show residual sugar. Mosel slate gives a smoky, stony note.
confusion: Alsace Riesling is drier and fuller; Australian Riesling is dry with lime and lower in residual sugar; Chenin Blanc has wax and quince.

description: Lemon, lime, green apple and peach with petrol, flint and wet stone. Drier and fuller-bodied than German Riesling.
notes: Grand Cru examples are powerful and mineral; most are dry or with only slight residual sugar.
confusion: German Riesling is lighter with more residual sugar; Alsace Pinot Gris is richer with lower acid.

region: Clare Valley & Eden Valley, South Australia
description: Intense lime, lime zest and grapefruit with lime blossom, early petrol and talc. Bone-dry with laser-like acidity.
notes: Petrol notes appear early because of strong sunlight. Almost always dry.
confusion: German Riesling usually shows residual sugar and lower alcohol; Albariño lacks the petrol.

description: Grapefruit, lemon, gooseberry and green apple with cut grass, flint, chalk and gunsmoke. Lean and racy.
notes: Silex (flint) soils in Pouilly-Fumé and Sancerre add smoky minerality. Usually no oak.
confusion: New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc is far more tropical and pungent; Chablis lacks the herbaceousness.

description: Lemon, grapefruit and white peach with fresh herbs, beeswax from Sémillon, and toast and vanilla from new oak. Rounder and fuller than Loire.
notes: Blended with Sémillon and aged in new wood.
confusion: Burgundy Chardonnay lacks the herbaceous note; California Fumé Blanc is riper with lower acid.

description: Ripe grapefruit, melon, white peach and lemongrass with a subtle grassy note and some vanilla or cream from oak (Fumé Blanc).
notes: Styles range from stainless-steel fresh to barrel-fermented Fumé Blanc.
confusion: New Zealand is more pungent and acidic; Bordeaux blanc shows more wax and higher acid.

description: Pungent passion fruit, grapefruit, lime and gooseberry with jalapeño, green bell pepper, cut grass and tomato leaf. Zesty and very aromatic.
notes: Usually stainless steel, no oak. High UV and cool nights give intense aromatics.
confusion: Loire Sauvignon Blanc is more mineral and restrained; Albariño lacks the pyrazine.

description: Peach, lemon and lychee with intense orange blossom, jasmine and rose, plus a soapy, bitter, pithy finish. Aromatic yet dry.
notes: High-altitude Salta (Cafayate) gives the most aromatic examples.
confusion: Gewurztraminer is fuller and oilier with more lychee and rose; Viognier is richer with lower acid.

description: Ripe apricot, peach, mango and tangerine with honeysuckle, violet and ginger. Oily and full-bodied with low acidity.
notes: Often aged partly in older oak. Aromatics fade quickly with age.
confusion: Gewurztraminer has more lychee and rose; California Chardonnay has more oak and butter; Torrontés is lighter and more bitter.
